core_obligations: Decompose [X'] and [Y'] as sums over the locally constant functions n_{x'} and n_{y'} and reduce to the case where X', X, Y', Y are delta-equidimensional with common values n', n, m', m satisfying n' - m' = n - m (proof lines 13671-13687).

Choose a factorization f = g o i with i an immersion and g smooth, shrink so that g has constant relative dimension and i is a closed immersion, and base change it along Y' -> Y to obtain i' : X' -> Y' x_Y P (proof lines 13689-13698).

Verify that the Cohen-Macaulay hypothesis survives the base change: for a generic point xi' of X' the local ring O_{Y' x_Y P, i'(xi')} is Cohen-Macaulay because the local map O_{Y', f'(xi)} -> O_{Y' x_Y P, i'(xi')} is flat with regular fibre, regular local rings are Cohen-Macaulay and Cohen-Macaulayness goes up along such a map (proof lines 13699-13710).
Conclude the reduced case f a regular closed immersion directly from the easier Gysin lemma (proof lines 13712-13718).
proof_roadmap: Split the fundamental classes along the locally constant dimension functions and reduce to the delta-equidimensional case (proof lines 13670-13687).
Factor f through a smooth map preceded by an immersion and base change the factorization to Y' (proof lines 13689-13698).
Transport the Cohen-Macaulay hypothesis through the flat map with regular fibres (proof lines 13699-13710) and quote the regular-closed-immersion case (proof lines 13712-13718).
difficulty_reason: The lemma is stated for a cartesian square of schemes locally of finite type over a fixed base situation, under four hypotheses: f is a local complete intersection morphism for which the Gysin map exists, all four schemes satisfy the equidimensionality conditions of a preceding lemma, the numerical condition n_{x'} - n_{y'} = n_x - n_y holds pointwise, and the local rings of Y' at the images of generic points of X' are Cohen-Macaulay; the conclusion is f^![Y'] = [X'] (statement lines 13642-13668). The proof requires first decomposing the fundamental classes as sums over the locally constant functions x' -> n_{x'}, etc. and reducing to the equidimensional case (proof lines 13670-13687), then choosing a factorization f = g o i with i an immersion and g smooth, base changing it to Y', and verifying that the Cohen-Macaulay hypothesis survives the base change by combining flatness of a smooth map, the fact that regular local rings are Cohen-Macaulay, and Cohen-Macaulayness going up along a flat local homomorphism with regular fibre (proof lines 13689-13710). The final case is a regular closed immersion, where the assertion is quoted from the easier Gysin lemma (proof line 13717). The reduction and the base-change verification of the Cohen-Macaulay condition are the non-formal content, so the claim is H2.
